briefing: A new face. Before you ride anywhere, go and see the smith. A bare sabre wins no wars.
I hear you.
Nothing lasts forever. Every piece of gear wears out with use, so read what the smith tells you about it before you pay.
Thank you for the warning.
A courtesy costs nothing and pays well. When a mission is done, pay a call on one of the generals you have met.
Good counsel. I will follow it.
Tap the direction twice and your legs will carry you twice as fast.
A dash forward. That will come in handy.
The smith lays out different wares before every mission.
Then I will look in on him after every mission, so I miss nothing.
The smith can forge a charm into your gear, but the fire is fickle. If the work fails, the piece is gone.
So I should think twice about what I put in his fire.
If a mission looks too hard for you, take another road. There is always another road.
I can always come back to it when I am stronger.
One visit, one mission. You cannot knock on two doors after a single fight.
Then I had better choose whose door it is.
Your pack holds forty-five things. Sell what you do not need to the smith before it fills up.
Then no good find will be left lying in the field.
That is all you need for now. Come back later and I will tell you more.
Thank you.
When you call on a general, do not always talk about the same thing. Try a new subject now and then.
The wider the talk, the more I learn.
Once you have crossed sabres with someone, there is no walking away. One of you leaves the field, and one of you stays on it.
Understood. Whoever stands in my way will not live to tell of it.
The road you take across the field decides whom you meet on it.
So with a little cunning I can keep clear of those I am not yet ready for.
A big field has many roads. Pick yours with care.
If one road is bad, I will try another.
Cross a warrior as an enemy today, and do not expect him to call you friend tomorrow.
Then I must weigh whom I fight.
Not everything worth having is sold by the smith. Plenty lies in the field for the man who looks.
So some things can only be found in the middle of a mission.
Watch the red ball and the blue one: your health and your spirit. Drink before it is too late.
I will keep a potion close at hand.
Put your potions on the belt before you set out. In the thick of a fight there is no time to dig through your pack.
Then my belt will never be empty.
On Normal, auto-hunt will fight for you. Take the sabre back yourself when things get hot.
So I can rest my arm and still keep watch.
The points you put into your stats can be taken back, but it will cost you gold or a tincture.
Then I will spend them wisely the first time.
Call on as many generals as you can. They say a guest brings luck into the house, and takes some away with him.
I hear they can teach a skill or put a charm on a blade too.
Do not leave anyone on your list without a visit.
So calling rarely puts me at a disadvantage?
Finish quickly and the mission pays you more experience for it.
Then I must strike fast and not dawdle.
Cut down the enemy archers first. Everything after that goes easier.
And a cleared field brings extra experience besides.
Every camp has a town hall. Look in on the colonels there: they keep count of what you have done for them.
Then I will see how far I have come with each of them.
The road you take will lead you to your fate. Choose it with your eyes open!
Fate favours the brave!
Your hero is saved each time he comes into a camp.
Then a lost mission will not cost me my whole road.
If the fighting feels slow to you, change the speed in the settings.
I will try that. A different pace may suit me better.
map: I do not know your face. Name yourself!
Step aside and yield, or taste my sabre!
Last chance: lower that sabre, or I will take it from you!
Have we met? Who are you?
Have it your way. Let the sabres talk!
You have no manners at all. Die!
My name does not matter. Enough talk. Prepare yourself!
A warrior worth the name lets his steel do the talking.
A bad day. I had hoped never to meet you across a field.
How can you raise your sabre against me, &?
Of all the people to meet here... but I have my orders, and so have you.
Ha... you are no match for me!
It cannot be! Why would you fight me, &?
Our fate is in our sabres now...
To raise a hand against each other brings only grief. Why has God sent me such a trial, &...
Fate has dealt us a bad hand, but I will play it.
God forgive me, brother. My hand will do what my heart cannot.
general: You handle yourself well, warrior. Better than most.
Drop in on me some time.
Not much of a talker, are you? We will meet again, I think.
You are better than they told me.
Let me stand you a jug some day.
Mark my words, and come by soon.
That is real skill!
Come over for a jug and we will talk.
The silent sort, I see. Think on my invitation. Farewell for now.
A mercy that your sabre is with us and not against us!
Until next time, warrior!
Hmm...
My door is open to you whenever you care to knock.
Good to see you again.
Come and share a jug with me. I would enjoy the company.
Hmm...
God go with you, warrior.
You are a great warrior, no doubt about it!
Thank you.
It would honour me to drink with you.
Hmm...
Ha-ha... think it over. Farewell till then!
This is an honour!
No, the honour is mine.
Come and sit at my table some evening. I would count it a favour.
Thank you for the warm words.
See you there, then!
Impressive! Few men fight with your courage.
And fewer lead men the way you do, general.
Do me the honour of a jug of ale with me.
Gladly.
I will be waiting.
You fight like a god, hero!
You are too kind.
I insist: you must come and drink with me.
To that I will drink!
Then I look forward to it.
You are a living legend...
No. Only a plain warrior.
Nonsense. You will be the guest of honour in my house.
The honour is all mine.
Good! Until then, brother.
